To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
supervisors’ security provision is associated with positive employee work-related outcomes, mediated by closeness and meaning.
supervisor security provision is associated with positive work outcomes, which are mediated by employees' closeness behaviors and, for same-sex supervisors, employees' sense of work meaning.

supervisors who provide employees with attachment security (i.e., a sense of being cared for and supported by the supervisor) are more likely to be close to their employees, and this closeness is associated with employees' sense of work meaning, which in turn is associated with positive work outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of attachment security in the supervisor-subordinate relationship.
the role of attachment in the workplace and how attachment theory can help us understand the nature of the employee-supervisor relationship.
the role of the supervisor in the attachment system of the employee.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the supervisor security provision is associated with several work related outcomes, which is mediated by closeness behavior and employees' sense of meaningful work.

supervisors who are able to provide a sense of attachment security to their subordinates are able to create a work environment where the subordinates are more committed, satisfied, less burned out, and more productive.
the attachment style of the supervisor is a significant factor in the relationship with the employee.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

supervisors' provision of a secure base for their subordinates may promote employees' positive work-related outcomes by enhancing closeness behaviors in their relationship and, in the case of same-sex supervisors and subordinates, by promoting a sense of meaning in the work.
attachment theory can provide a framework for understanding how employees and supervisors relate to one another.
attachment theory can provide a useful lens through which to examine supervisor security provision and its effects on employee outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
employees are more likely to experience positive outcomes in their work if they perceive their supervisors as being responsive to their needs and available when needed.
supervisors can influence employees' attachment security, which in turn can have positive outcomes for employees.
employees who perceive their supervisors as providing attachment-related security report more positive outcomes, such as job satisfaction, organizational identification, and performance.
